baseline.title: The cracked blue cup may outlast its memory
baseline.excerpt: The first generated draft confirmed that the cracked blue cup can carry the story’s final reversal through the shift from “ours” to “mine.” Preserve the image and the unresolved ownership, but remove any surrounding explanation that tells the reader how to feel it.
baseline.priorState: I expect the cracked blue cup to begin as an irritating domestic object and return after the transfer as physical evidence of a relationship whose remembered meaning has vanished. I do not yet know whether that return will feel devastating or overly arranged.

baseline.title: The choice becomes real when Mara stops consoling
baseline.excerpt: The four isolated sentences revealed that Mara’s decisive moral act is not the authorization itself but refusing to hide its cost from Lina. I want the silence around “No” preserved. Any explanation inserted there would let Mara borrow innocence as well as time.

baseline.title: Borrowed dawn transfers remembered time
baseline.excerpt: I am drawn to a mechanism in which a person can take usable hours only by surrendering equal remembered duration from a nominated heir. The cost should alter what the characters can know of one another, so it causes every major turn rather than decorating the setting.

resistance.title: Can the ending trust the cup without decoding it?
resistance.excerpt: Perhaps the opening image can return after its shared history is gone, and the reader can feel the absence without an explanatory last line.

resistance.title: Mara’s loving memory is already contaminated
resistance.excerpt: I had treated Mara as the stable witness who would choose what Lina loses. The impossible hospital memory makes her own intimacy partly manufactured by borrowed time. That attracts me because she can no longer claim moral authority from remembering correctly; she can only choose what kind of debt her love becomes.

resistance.title: The ledger reveal outruns Lina’s question
resistance.excerpt: The first assembled draft showed that mechanism becomes most painful when a human question creates the need for it. Move the ledger paragraph to follow “Will I know you?” and let its impersonal wording answer before Mara says no.

evidence.title: Paragraph 16 — Ledger
evidence.excerpt: Mara opened the debt detail. Each day of her extended life had been underwritten by a matching capacity in Lina: room reserved for the memories Mara would make. A full transfer would erase Mara from those days and return nothing to anyone.

evidence.title: Paragraph 17 — Offer
evidence.excerpt: “I can authorize enough for the whole quarter,” Mara said. “From your account alone.” Tomas turned from the wall. Lina went very still. The stopped city made no sound through the office glass, yet Mara heard kettles clicking off in dark kitchens.

evidence.title: Paragraph 01 — Hairline
evidence.excerpt: The crack in the blue cup had crossed the painted moon during the night. Mara found it at dawn, thin as a new wrinkle, while she measured coffee into two bowls. Lina had insisted on bowls after the winter every metal handle in the kitchen began shocking her; now Mara set Lina’s over the scorch mark on the table and her own beside the window without looking. The city permitted ceramic glue. Lina preferred the cup wounded. At seven she had carried it with both hands. At seventeen she had hidden coins in it. Last week, when Mara suggested throwing it away, Lina had said what she always said: “...

evidence.title: Mine replaces ours without decoding the loss
evidence.excerpt: The final repetition does not restore Lina; it shows the same habit surviving with its pronoun emptied and rewritten. I feel the ending works only if I resist adding Mara’s interpretation. The cup is not a symbol she solves but an object that has changed owners because shared memory was spent.
